title: Give recurring decisions a fast path

chapters.title: One more ticket. Another model read.
chapters.text: One customer. Two charges. Your application asks the model which team should handle the ticket. The answer is billing.

chapters.title: Same answer. A much shorter route.
chapters.text: A small CPU fast path can return familiar answers. For short texts, embedding and classification take about fifty microseconds.

chapters.title: New wording. A familiar decision.
chapters.text: Different words can lead to the same decision. A learned classifier recognizes the recurring task, beyond exact text repeats.

chapters.title: Unfamiliar? Keep decisio in the loop.
chapters.text: Not every request qualifies. Pass those requests to decisio. The model stays available, and the application keeps its answer interface.

chapters.title: First, learn from examples.
chapters.text: Teach from human-labelled requests, or collect model answers. These examples train a small candidate for one recurring decision.

chapters.title: Check it before it answers.
chapters.text: Check separate examples and the saving on your host. Activate only a candidate that qualifies. Otherwise, keep the model path.

chapters.title: Keep the rules. Send the new facts.
chapters.text: Register shared rules once as context. Send changing facts as state. The classifier reads facts; the model gets both.

chapters.title: Route support tickets as they arrive.
chapters.text: Route recurring billing and access requests on the CPU. Keep unfamiliar support requests on the model path.

chapters.title: Sort new posts as they arrive.
chapters.text: Moderation works the same way. Keep the policy fixed, classify each new post, and send ambiguous cases to the model.

chapters.title: Check each return against the policy.
chapters.text: For refunds, keep the policy fixed. Send delivery age and item condition. Answer yes or no; pass exceptions on.

chapters.title: Keep the same task. Send fresh facts.
chapters.text: Register the task, shared context and fast table option. Ask with the same task identifier and new facts.

chapters.title: Give recurring decisions a fast path.
chapters.text: Let familiar decisions take the shorter route. Keep the model for everything else. Start with one task, and see what qualifies.
